target_customer: Indonesian ecommerce and direct-to-retail businesses selling chilled and frozen products, including retailers in the Aprindo association
problem: Cold chain products in Indonesia lack hyperlocal storage, pick and pack and delivery, making fast ecommerce fulfillment hard.
business_model: Fulfillment as a service: network of hyperlocal cold chain fulfillment centers, transport and a fulfillment management system, charged per storage and handling

founders.name: Larry Ridwan
founders.background_notes: YC page: about 20 years of work experience; says he received Indonesia's medal of honor for national development contributions (self-described)

founders.name: Widijastoro Nugroho
founders.background_notes: YC page: 25 years of experience including HoReCa ice cream and frozen products, airline launch, and media trading head

founders.name: Andre Septiano
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in DealStreetAsia and DailySocial coverage, not on the YC page

competitors.name: Segari
competitors.what: Fresh groceries sourced from farmers with neighborhood agents and last mile delivery

competitors.name: Sayurbox
competitors.what: Online fresh produce delivery with own supply chain

technical_complexity.rationale: Warehouse management software plus physical cold storage network operations across many sites.

defensibility.rationale: Capital-heavy network of cold hubs and retailer integrations is slow to copy, but customers can switch logistics providers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The e-grocers are customers and rivals rather than copycats; no source shows an incumbent copying or buying Fresh Factory.

market_need_then: Pandemic ecommerce boom and 2021 funding into Indonesian e-grocery created demand for cold chain fulfillment; East Ventures published an analysis calling cold chain the next opportunity for Indonesian logistics.

branding.brand_signature: Kulkas Berjalan (walking refrigerator) nickname used in detik coverage
branding.community_and_virality: Regular press coverage in Indonesian business media and an Aprindo retail association partnership; no merch or fan evidence

brand_strength.rationale: Clear, descriptive name with trade press recognition but generic and no evidence of brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Fresh Factory rode Indonesia's pandemic ecommerce growth, raised a $4.5M seed in June 2022 led by East Ventures and about $4.15M in April 2023 led by SBI Ven Capital, and expanded to dozens of fulfillment centers with retail partnerships. No Series A, shutdown or exit was found; scale claims vary widely across sources.
notes: freshfactory.id could not be read (page returned only a title); site treated as unverified. The 2023 round is called pre-Series A by sources, recorded as other. DailySocial reports an initial $1.5M in January 2021 (Prasetia Dwidharma, Numbers Capital, YC), seen in one outlet only so unverified and not recorded. Bisnis names SBI Ven Capital as lead while CB Insights lists East Ventures; DailySocial and DealStreetAsia agree on SBI Ven. Totals vary ($8.65M to $10.1M). Headcount varies between 100 and about 190.
